boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on campus-adjacent Chico corridors, each paired with one directly sourced reason to stop.

cards.title: Read Chico Through Its Artifacts
cards.subtitle: Salem Street at West 2nd Street
cards.notes: Cross onto Salem Street and examine the museum’s changing galleries plus permanent displays about the Mechoopda and Bidwells.
cards.short_summary: A campus-edge museum housed in Chico’s historic Carnegie library building.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is immediately adjacent to the university and presents changing exhibitions alongside permanent Mechoopda, Bidwell, Chinese Temple, and regional displays.
cards.access_notes: Located at 141 Salem Street. Open Thursday–Sunday, 11 a.m.–4 p.m.; confirm current exhibitions before visiting.

cards.title: See a Museum Devoted to Yo-Yos
cards.subtitle: Broadway Street between West 3rd and West 4th streets
cards.notes: Walk south on Broadway and enter through Bird in Hand to view the museum’s public display of yo-yos and related memorabilia.
cards.short_summary: A specialized downtown collection tucked inside a Broadway Street shop.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Yo-Yo Museum is located at 320 Broadway Street inside Bird in Hand and features a large public display of yo-yos and yo-yo memorabilia.
cards.access_notes: The listed hours are Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m. and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; enter through Bird in Hand.

cards.title: Try the Hands-On Exhibits
cards.subtitle: Main Street between East 3rd and East 4th streets
cards.notes: Head to Main Street with a child and plan time for exhibits designed to be touched, explored, and used for interactive play.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on museum designed primarily for children ages zero through twelve.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is at 325 Main Street, and its official FAQ says exhibits are intended for touching and interactive exploration.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions — Chico Children's Museum
cards.access_notes: Adults may enter only when accompanying a child unless an adult tour is approved and scheduled in advance.

cards.title: Pause Beneath the Plaza Trees
cards.subtitle: West 4th Street between Main Street and Broadway
cards.notes: Follow West 4th Street to the full-block public plaza and use its shaded walkways as a downtown pause between destinations.
cards.short_summary: A civic green occupying the downtown block bounded by four central streets.
cards.evidence_claim: A City of Chico historic-resource record identifies City Plaza as the block bounded by 4th, 5th, Main, and Broadway and describes its shade trees and walkways.
cards.source_title: West Numbered Streets Historic Resources Inventory
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor public park. Areas are first-come, first-served unless posted as reserved for an event.

cards.entity_name: Chico Certified Farmers’ Market — Saturday Market
cards.title: Meet Growers at the Saturday Market
cards.subtitle: Wall Street at East 2nd Street
cards.notes: Take East 2nd Street to Wall Street on Saturday morning and browse the year-round certified market directly from its vendors.
cards.short_summary: A recurring downtown market with farmers and vendors selling directly to shoppers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chico Certified Farmers’ Market operates its year-round Saturday market at the Downtown Chico Municipal Parking Lot at 2nd and Wall streets.
cards.access_notes: Open Saturdays year-round, rain or shine, from 7:30 a.m.–1 p.m. Browsing requires no admission; purchases are optional.

cards.title: Catch an Independent Film
cards.subtitle: East 6th Street between Flume and Orient streets
cards.notes: Continue to East 6th Street and check the Pageant’s current program for an arthouse, independent, documentary, or world-cinema screening.
cards.short_summary: A small downtown cinema focused on films beyond mainstream multiplex programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pageant Theatre at 351 East 6th Street presents arthouse films, independent movies, documentaries, world cinema, and classic films.
cards.access_notes: Screenings follow the theater’s current program. Check the film rating and showtime before going; admission requires a ticket.

cards.title: Stock Up at the Downtown Co-op
cards.subtitle: Main Street between East 8th and East 9th streets
cards.notes: Follow Main Street south to the cooperative for groceries; note the daily 10 p.m. closing time when planning an evening supply run.
cards.short_summary: A downtown consumer cooperative with daily morning-to-night access.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico Natural Foods Cooperative is located at 818 Main Street and is open daily from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7 a.m.–10 p.m. Entry is open to shoppers; merchandise and prepared food require purchase.

cards.title: Check the Current Gallery Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Orange Street beside the historic rail depot
cards.notes: Walk west to Orange Street and check the gallery during posted daytime hours; pair the stop with a look at the depot setting.
cards.short_summary: A community art center occupying space beside Chico’s historic railway depot.
cards.evidence_claim: Chico Art Center is located at 450 Orange Street, Suite 6, and publishes daytime gallery hours Tuesday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday 11:30 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; listed holiday closures apply.

cards.title: See Northern California Art
cards.subtitle: The Esplanade at East Washington Avenue
cards.notes: Head north on The Esplanade and review the current exhibition list before visiting this museum devoted to Northern California art.
cards.short_summary: A regional art museum presenting rotating exhibitions in a landmark building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Northern California Art is located at 900 Esplanade and describes itself as a showcase and vehicle for Northern California artists and the community.
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday–Sunday 11 a.m.–5 p.m. Check the museum’s current exhibition and admission information before departure.

cards.title: Browse a Volunteer-Run Gallery
cards.subtitle: Park Avenue at West 17th Street
cards.notes: Continue down the Park Avenue corridor during gallery hours and inspect the current visual-art installation before exploring nearby stops.
cards.short_summary: A volunteer-supported space for visual art and multidisciplinary cultural events.
cards.evidence_claim: 1078 Gallery is located at 1710 Park Avenue and provides a venue for visual arts, music, theater, and literary events.
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours are Friday–Sunday 10 a.m.–2 p.m. Event access and charges may vary; check the current calendar before visiting.
